描述_ZN: The "Kong Biao Stele", ink topography of the whole paper stele Yang (the front and back of the stele are missing topography), mounted on a vertical axis. It measures 199 cm in length and 85.5 cm in width. It is written in 18 lines of official script, with 45 characters.　　Confucius Biao, with the character Yuan Shang, was the nineteenth grandson of Confucius and lived in the late Eastern Han Dynasty. At the beginning, he was promoted to the position of filial integrity, and was removed from the position of governor and Bo Chang Chang. Later, he served as a minister of the Shang Shu, a royal official, a governor of Boling, a minister of Xiapi, and a governor of Hedong. He resigned due to illness and retired. He died in the seventh month of the fourth year of Jianning in the Eastern Han Dynasty (171) at the age of 49. This monument was erected by 13 people, including Cui Lie, a former official (the title is on the shade of the monument) to praise his legacy. The original stone is now in the Confucius Temple in Qufu, Shandong Province.　　The inscription is simple and elegant, and can be regarded as a standard example of Eastern Han inscriptions. The inscription is written in the middle of a boundary grid, and the characters are small, but the spacing between characters and lines is extremely wide, making the layout clear and transparent. Yang Shoujing's "Hormone Feiqingge Review of Stele" says that his characters are "strong in strokes and strict in structure", which is the most definite comment. It has been listed as one of the most famous Han clerical works. It is a pity that the characters are more corroded and damaged.　　The character "Ying" in the fifth line and the character "Life" in the sixth line have been lost, but The word "life" in the sixth line of "Sitting at home without destiny" has been lost, but is still legible. In the sixth line, the word "cut" in the character "to cut the four evils" can be seen as "small" on the left. In the fourteenth line, the character "辯" is half of the character "辯", and the character "居" is visible in the remaining strokes. It must be an old topography from the middle and early Qing dynasty. Inscriptions of "Zhang Delong Jianzang Jinshi Script" and "Sanqu Zhang's Jinshi Shoukao" are on two sides.　　Song Ouyang Xiu's "The End of the Jigu Record", Ouyang Nian's "The Catalogue of the Jigu Record", Zhao Mingcheng's "Jinshilu", Hong Shi's "The Interpretation of Clerical Script", Chen Si's "Collection of Treasure Carvings", Ming Yang Shen's "Jinshilu Ancient Writings", Du Mu's "Jinlian Linlang", Qing Sun Chengze's "Gengzi Pin Xia Ji", Gu Yanwu's "Jinshilu Writings", Weng Fanggang's "Jinshilu Writings of the Two Han Dynasties", Qian Daxin's "The End of the Jinshilu Writings of Qian Yan Tang", Ruan Yuan's "Shanzuo Jinshilu Zhi", modern Wang Chang's The Jin Shi Zu Zu Zui Editorial", Fang Ruo's "Sui Pian" and other books.
